extracted.intended_audience: software developers authoring or reviewing GitHub pull requests (code contributors and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors and reviewers to conduct faster, kinder, and higher-quality code reviews on pull requests (PRs), including what to look for, interaction norms, and procedural best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be respectful / Ask - Explain - Suggest
rubrics_metrics.description: Always be considerate and respectful in reviews: don't use the imperative, don't judge, don't blame (don't curse), don't be arrogant, don't use sarcasm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of ordering or blaming, ask questions assuming everyone is intelligent and well-meaning; explicitly explain your point of view even if verbose; make suggestions. Respect, humility, and clarity reduce friction and speed resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop the 'reply' hemorrhage / Offer to talk in person
rubrics_metrics.description: Many replies to a comment indicate miscommunication; excessive back-and-forth creates noise and frustration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discussion spirals, offer to talk in person or pair-program to resolve; after the conversation, post a concise summary to the PR to share the agreement with everyone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer encouragement & appreciation / Give positive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Code reviews should not only point out mistakes but also highlight good practices and congratulate good work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Say simple positive things like 'thank you', 'great', 'nice' when appropriate — positive feedback improves motivation and team dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agree on a coding style / Automate
rubrics_metrics.description: Coding style debates are often subjective; teams should agree on a style and automate enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formatters and linters to remove personal taste from reviews so reviewers can focus on correctness and design rather than style nitpicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: And the first reviewer is... you! / Assess your code
rubrics_metrics.description: Before inviting reviewers, the author should self-review their own changes to catch inconsistencies, mistakes, or simpler solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review changes outside your IDE and consider edge cases; self-review reduces trivial comments and speeds the overall process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be proactive / Provide context
rubrics_metrics.description: For complex PRs, authors should write a general comment explaining purpose, overview of changes, and rationale for choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight the most important parts of a large change; providing context helps reviewers understand intent and reduces questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wait for the green light
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't invite reviewers while CI/tests are failing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wait until the pipeline passes to avoid the first comment being 'build is failing' and wasting reviewers' time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Select reviewers based on who should see the changes, who will be impacted, who has time, and who is qualified to give feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think about visibility, impact, availability, and expertise before adding people to a PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose the right number of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Be inclusive but avoid too many reviewers which can create conflicting directions or diffusion of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a few core reviewers to get main feedback, then add others for visibility as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep it small / Divide and conquer
rubrics_metrics.description: Small, focused PRs are reviewed faster and more thoroughly than large ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize work into a series of simpler PRs; a rule-of-thumb: 10 lines -> 10 issues; 500 lines -> 'looks fine.' Break big changes into multiple PRs when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rome wasn't built in a day / Create new tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: If a review uncovers large refactors or substantial additional work, create a new task instead of blocking the current PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to the new task in the review; this prevents long delays, reduces merge conflict risk, and keeps momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't take it personally / Keep an open mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat review comments as attempts to improve the codebase, not personal attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offended, ask for clarification, take distance, assume good intentions, and evaluate code objectively as if written by someone else.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify the code first / Help future developers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer doesn't understand code, the author should first try to clarify the code itself; if not possible, add explanatory code comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explaining in the review alone doesn't help future readers; prefer making code or inline comments clearer so future developers benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave this world a little better than you found it / The boy scout rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PRs as an opportunity to improve the codebase (tests, naming, small cleanups) even if not required for the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make small, intentional improvements rather than overhauling everything; improve long-term project health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer all comments / Write the end of the story
rubrics_metrics.description: Before closing a review, authors should respond to all comments to show respect and provide a clear conclusion to the dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responding helps reviewers and serves as a future reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice mindfulness / Love (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should approach reviews with calm and gratitude; short breathing/mantra exercises are suggested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt mindful phrasing and attitude (e.g., 'I vow to write code mindfully and lovingly') to foster constructive collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empathize / The other person is you
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should consider how their words will be received and write comments that are both helpful and kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pause and imagine your reaction to the comment; craft feedback with empathy to avoid harming collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid selective ownership / It's our code!
rubrics_metrics.description: Use inclusive language (we/our) rather than finger-pointing 'your'/'mine' to promote shared ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rephrase comments to show collaboration and shared responsibility for the codebase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide references
rubrics_metrics.description: Support comments with concrete references to help the author understand and act on feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include code samples, links to documentation, previous reviews, blog posts, or repositories when making suggestions; references also help other reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek the author's perspective / We always learn
rubrics_metrics.description: When something in the code is surprising, ask for the author's reasoning rather than assuming malice or incompetence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the author may know details you don't; seek their explanation before pushing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't be a gatekeeper / Improvements have a threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid creating never-ending cycles of requested changes; balance quality improvements against delivery and developer happiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide when a good increment is sufficient; review to provide feedback, not to block indefinitely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the best review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: If you don't feel qualified to review a part of the PR, invite someone who is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring in the right expertise so the author gets high-quality feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to look for — Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether interactions among code pieces make sense and whether the change integrates well with the codebase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: Is now a good time to add this functionality? Do design choices fit project architecture and future maintainability?

rubrics_metrics.name: What to look for — Functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm the code implements the author's intended behavior and that the behavior is appropriate for end users (both end-users and developers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify intent vs. implementation and consider whether the change serves user needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to look for — Complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether code is understandable, whether it invites bugs, or whether it's over-engineered for hypothetical future needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simpler solutions that solve current needs; avoid speculative complexity that increases maintenance burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to look for — Tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for appropriate unit tests that are correct, sensible, and useful; review tests first to understand author intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading tests can quickly reveal intended behavior; ensure tests exist and validate important cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to look for — Naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether names communicate purpose clearly: long enough to be descriptive but not so long as to harm readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good names reduce cognitive load; suggest renames that make intent clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to look for — Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether comments are clear and useful, and whether they explain 'why' or 'what' rather than 'how'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer comments that document rationale and intent; avoid redundant comments that only restate implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to look for — Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Check adherence to existing style, naming, and organizational agreements in the codebase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency aids maintainability; ensure changes follow established project conventions or document deliberate deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to look for — Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If code changes affect how users build, test, interact with, or release the project, verify relevant documentation is updated, removed, or added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation changes should accompany behavioral changes to avoid confusing future users and contributors.
